posts.author: PhantomPixel
posts.body:
Heya! So an RPG Maker character sheet that uses the $ symbol at the beginning, needs to be setup in a 3 x 4 type of grid. So for your particular sprite to work, you'll need to make your canvas 192 x 384. So it'll look something like this:
Then, when you try to select it in the engine, it should look right. Just make sure to remember the $ at the beginning of the filename!

because you not only need the rows, but also the columns.
A sprite with the symbol $ (the smallest possible) needs 3x4 cells, so you need that picture twelve times in the grid of 3x4.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Okay, there's a few things going on here!
First, events will always center on a single tile. You can work around this by splitting your character (painting, in this case) in half, and using one event for the left side and another event for the right side.
Second, sprites have a 6 pixel offset by default. It boosts the characters up so that they don't walk right on the bottom edge of the tile. You can get around this by adding a "!" to the beginning of the file name.
Avery covers how to use ! and $ in this tutorial!
Finally, the reason that $ didn't work for you is that even when you use $, you still need to have a whole character set--not just one frame. So you would need a document that's three times as wide and four times as tall as your painting (so 192 x 384 pixels) to get the whole painting in one frame.
Ninja'd by PhantomPixel, but my first point still holds true! Give me two shakes and I'll see if I can set up a sample the way I would do it.
